1.w: After five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and an attorney named Tertullus, and they brought formal charges against Paul to the governor.

2.w: When Paul had been summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “We have experienced a lengthy time of peace through your rule, and reforms are being made in this nation through your foresight.

3.w: Most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this everywhere and in every way with all gratitude.

4.w: But so that I may not delay you any further, I beg you to hear us briefly with your customary graciousness.

5.w: For we have found this man to be a troublemaker, one who stirs up riots among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

6.w: He even tried to desecrate the temple, so we arrested him.

8.w: When you examine him yourself, you will be able to learn from him about all these things we are accusing him of doing.”

9.w: The Jews also joined in the verbal attack, claiming that these things were true.

10.w: When the governor gestured for him to speak, Paul replied, “Because I know that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I confidently make my defense.

11.w: As you can verify for yourself, not more than 12 days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

12.w: They did not find me arguing with anyone or stirring up a crowd in the temple courts or in the synagogues or throughout the city,

13.w: nor can they prove to you the things they are accusing me of doing.

14.w: But I confess this to you, that I worship the God of our ancestors according to the Way (which they call a sect), believing everything that is according to the law and that is written in the prophets.

15.w: I have a hope in God (a hope that these men themselves accept too) that there is going to be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.

16.w: This is the reason I do my best to always have a clear conscience toward God and toward people.

17.w: After several years I came to bring to my people gifts for the poor and to present offerings,

18.w: which I was doing when they found me in the temple, ritually purified, without a crowd or a disturbance.

19.w: But there are some Jews from the province of Asia who should be here before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.

20.w: Or these men here should tell what crime they found me guilty of when I stood before the council,

21.w: other than this one thing I shouted out while I stood before them: ‘I am on trial before you today concerning the resurrection of the dead.’”

22.w: Then Felix, who understood the facts concerning the Way more accurately, adjourned their hearing, saying, “When Lysias the commanding officer comes down, I will decide your case.”

23.w: He ordered the centurion to guard Paul, but to let him have some freedom, and not to prevent any of his friends from meeting his needs.

24.w: Some days later, when Felix arrived with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

25.w: While Paul was discussing righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “Go away for now, and when I have an opportunity, I will send for you.”

26.w: At the same time he was also hoping that Paul would give him money, and for this reason he sent for Paul as often as possible and talked with him.

27.w: After two years had passed, Porcius Festus succeeded Felix, and because he wanted to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
